2. Learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner submitted that  this Court vide order dated 07.06.2021 in BLAPL No.1409 of 2021  passed the following order:-
 "***Considering the submission made by the learned  counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner in in judicial  custody since 02.10.2020 and he has been charge sheeted  under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal  Code read with section 6 of the POCSO Act and after  going through the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim, in  which she has stated about her love affairs with the  petitioner and leaving her lawful guardianship on her own  accord and staying in the house of the petitioner for about  a week and her further statement that she had no physical  relationship with the petitioner during her stay with him  Page 1 of 3  and further the fact that the victim refused for her medical  examination and after hearing the learned counsel for the  State, I am inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
 Let the petitioner be released on bail in the aforesaid  case on furnishing bail bond of Rs.50,000/- (rupees fifty  thousand) with two local solvent sureties each for the like  amount to the satisfaction of the Court in seisin over the  matter with further terms and conditions as the learned  Court may deem just and proper."

sentences.text: date of posting appeared before the learned Court, but on 05.05.2025 due to ill-health, communication could not be made to his counsel.
Therefore, he could not be represented before the learned ADJ-cum-FTSC(I), Jajpur.
Therefore, the learned court vide order dated 05.05.2025 issued Non-Bailable Warrant of arrest against the Petitioner.

3. Mr. Ashok Kumar Apat, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State-Opposite Party raising serious objection to the contention of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that as pendency of the matter was within the knowledge of the petitioner,
he should have appeared before the Court concerned and sought for the appropriate relief.

4. Heard Mr. Bijay Kumar Mohanty, learned counsel appearing for the Petitioner and Mr. Ashok Kumar Apat, learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the State.
5.

Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respective parties, this Court taking into consideration the order dated 07.06.2021 passed in BLAPL No.1409 of 2021, the order dated 05.05.2025 passed by the learned ADJ-cum-FTSC(I), Jajpur in C.T. No.1899 of 2020 (CT Spl.(P) 125/25) is hereby quashed.

The Petitioner is directed to surrender on or before 17th June,
2025 before the learned ADJ-cum-FTSC(I), Jajpur.
On his appearance the Court concerned shall proceed with the matter in accordance with law.

6. Needless to observe that in the event of default on the part of the accused to appear before the Court concerned as directed above, this order shall not be given effect to and the Court shall proceed as deemed fit and proper in accordance with law.
7.
In view of the above, the CRLMC stands disposed of.
(M.S. Raman) Vacation Judge Laxmikant Signed by: LAXMIKANT MOHAPATRA Designation:
